quizName: Hardest Questions in North carolina Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can touch your feet to the ground while sitting on it.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars go over your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch your feet to the ground while sitting on it.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly when your feet can touch the ground while you sit on it. You should be able to reach and operate all the controls easily.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of having an accident, you should:

options.text: Try to blend in with traffic and not be noticed by other drivers.
Only use turn signals when driving at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
Ride very close to the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Signal your moves with turn signals and brake lights. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Look ahead 12 seconds and be ready to react to any hazards.

questions.question: To get the most protection from a helmet, choose one that:

options.text: Has been in a previous crash.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards for the best protection. The helmet should fit snugly all the way around your head.

questions.question: A danger of riding next to parked cars is:

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Other drivers may be going slowly while looking for parking.
The road surface may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Riding next to parked cars is dangerous. A driver might pull out of a space into your path without looking. Car doors may open into your lane, and pedestrians may step out between cars.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles allows you to:

options.text: Have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Stay in one spot in the lane and limit your movement.
Depend on other drivers to find hazards.
Go faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can improve visibility by:
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing with reflective materials so other drivers can see you. Always use your headlight, and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible across it.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries can be prevented by:
questions.explanation: Wearing a good-quality helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. A helmet is the best protection a rider has in case of an accident.

questions.question: Which fabric gives the most protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants provide the best protection when riding a motorcycle.

questions.question: The best source for information about your motorcycle is:
questions.explanation: Your owner's manual is the best source for information about your specific motorcycle. It includes details about how it works, its features, and maintenance.

questions.question: What types of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-certified helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who rides a different motorcycle

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding and hope you wake up

questions.explanation: Do not ride when you are tired. On long trips, take a rest break at least every two hours to avoid fatigue.

questions.question: What removes alcohol and its effects from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time reduces your blood alcohol content (BAC). Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change how much alcohol is in your body.

questions.question: Which surface is slippery and hard to control on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted markings, and metal covers in the road. Ride slowly and carefully on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: What should a rider always watch for ahead on the road?
questions.explanation: Look ahead to notice changes in traffic, hazards on the road, and possible escape routes. Be ready to react quickly to any changes.

questions.question: Which color helps you be seen while riding?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green while riding. Bright clothing makes you easier to see at any time of day.

questions.question: Which organization certifies helmets for maximum protection?
questions.explanation: Use a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards for the best protection.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you turn or change lanes. Do this even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: Your friend has drunk too much alcohol and wants to ride their motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads.

questions.explanation: Never let someone ride if they have been drinking. Do whatever you need to stop them, including taking their keys. Help them find another way to get home.

questions.question: How does your body get rid of alcohol?
questions.explanation: Your body can only remove alcohol by taking time. There is no quick way to become sober.

questions.question: What material are motorcycle riding gloves usually made from?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: If your shoes have laces, what should you do with them while riding?
questions.explanation: Tuck your shoe laces in tightly while riding. This keeps them from catching on your motorcycle.
